"Score the card 1-5 on each criterion. For each score give ref, the card line (card:<field>) that decides it, or plan:<field path> when no card line carries it, and a reason of at most 25 words. Use NA only where a criterion allows it. Then name decides_by: the id of the earliest phase after which decision_rule can be applied whichever outcome occurs, or \"none\". A phase that only reproduces a published number, or only measures throughput the question does not ask about, does not count. Give decides_by_reason in at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Root question: Can molecular mapping of AAV capsid-receptor interactions on brain microvascular endothelial cells determine which AAV variants transcytose across the blood-brain barrier versus remain intracellular, and for which capsid-receptor binding signatures?
Option record: {\"id\":\"V3\",\"title\":\"Motif calls emitted for Capsida NR001–NR005 and Lir Starfish binding-assay readouts\",\"summary\":\"Enumerate binding modes of capsid libraries against the human BBB-receptor set used by Capsida's NR001–NR005 platform and Lir's Starfish capsid-structure pipeline (ALPL, AAVR, LRP6 and their panel partners) with docking, MD refinement and AlphaFold-Multimer, emitting calls in the format of plate- and bead-based capsid–receptor binding assays. Score whether 3-fold-axis engagement geometry agrees with measured bind/no-bind receptor by receptor, then rank the binding-positive pairs as the only candidates worth a transcytosis claim. Published modeling covers only single-digit complexes, and neither Capsida's nor Lir's structural pipeline has been assessed against exhaustive enumeration. Narrowing: Leaves aside transcytosis and all post-binding fate — the observable is binding agreement plus interface geometry, not fate. It still moves the root question by narrowing the candidate signature catalog (Q3) to pairs that survive a human-receptor binding assay, which is the precondition for any sufficiency test (Q1).\",\"root_link\":\"Bears on Q3 of the root question — which capsid–receptor binding signatures are candidates for transcytosis — by pruning the catalog to pairs that survive a real human-receptor binding assay before any transcytosis claim (Q1) is attempted.\",\"compute_open\":\"More parallel compute buys model runs across capsid × receptor × pose for the NR001–NR005 receptor set, letting the shared-motif question be tested receptor by receptor against binding readouts rather than at a single receptor; published depth effects stop at single-digit complexes and the proprietary pipelines are unmeasured, so the payoff is unknown.\",\"sequential\":\"none: each capsid–receptor pose is an independent docking or AlphaFold-Multimer job with its own seeds, and the plate/bead binding readouts are a separate block.\",\"source_urls\":[]}
Card:
card:question: Can computed capsid–receptor binding calls for ALPL, AAVR and LRP6 reproduce published bind/no-bind readouts with interfaces at the threefold axis?
card:hypothesis: Pairs that bind in plate- and bead-based assays share threefold-axis or insert-loop engagement geometry, so pose enumeration recovers published bind/no-bind labels [s_aavr_struct].
card:sequential_part: No answer waits on another: 216 independent runs; three stages follow one another only within each run.
card:method: none
card:if_lever: Balanced accuracy 0.80 at 432 runs versus 0.55 at 54, with five of six known binders within 5 Å of published sites.
card:if_not: Accuracy moves under 0.05 between 54 and 432 runs and at most three of six binders reach published sites; extra runs resample the wrong basin.
card:test_summary: Thirty-six capsid–receptor pairs run docking, three AlphaFold-Multimer seeds, two 5-ns MD relaxations; calls and threefold-site geometry scored on published labels; parallel wall-clock versus serial one-GPU and independent-copy baselines.
card:closest_prior: Shay and colleagues in 2024 ran five AlphaFold-Multimer models per peptide and used cryo-ET to map where LRP6 and IL3 bind engineered capsids, with SPR binding labels [s_shay_af].
card:left_open: Whether hundreds of pose and seed runs improve bind/no-bind agreement with threefold-axis geometry across a full capsid-by-receptor grid remains untested [s_shay_af].
card:anchor: Redocking AAVR-PKD2 onto AAV2 must place it beside the threefold spike matching PDB 6IHB contacts; serial and parallel pilots must match calls.
card:limits: Binding-call agreement and interface geometry only; no transcytosis or affinity. Public labels cover 13 of 36 pairs; NR001–NR005 and Starfish assays are proprietary.
